review_candidates.title: Senior GNC / Systems Integration Engineer
review_candidates.description: About Portal Portal Space Systems is on a mission to expand humanity’s freedom of movement in space. We’re building the spacecraft that makes that mission possible. From our Bothell, WA headquarters, we design vehicles with the maneuverability, resilience, and adaptability needed for the next era of orbital operations. Every system we build is in service of a simple idea: space should be more accessible, responsive, and capable. Joining Portal means stepping into a team that believes in bold engineering, fast iteration, and the power of small groups to change what’s possible. If you want your work to directly shape the future of in-space mobility, join us. Role Overview The Senior GNC / Systems Integration Engineer bridges GNC, spacecraft systems engineering, flight software, and test. The role owns GNC requirements flow-down and verification, supports integration of GNC sensors and actuators, and leads GNC participation in integration, testing, and operations preparation. This position works closely with systems engineering, flight software, electrical, avionics, and AIT, and is accountable for verification closure, GNC test execution, flight software integration, and operational readiness. Core Responsibilities Own GNC requirements flow-down from mission and system requirements to subsystem, component, and flight software requirements. Own the GNC verification matrix, test plans, and acceptance criteria, and drive verification to closure. Support integration of star trackers, IMUs, reaction wheels, propulsion systems, and other GNC hardware, including avionics testing. Define GNC flight software requirements, mode transitions, telemetry, and fault management implementation with flight software engineers. Lead GNC participation in FlatSat, software-in-the-loop, hardware-in-the-loop, environmental, TVAC, and spacecraft integrated testing. Perform polarity, phasing, and functional checks of GNC sensors and actuators. Analyze test data, investigate anomalies, and track issues to closure. Develop GNC flight rules, operations procedures, telemetry monitoring, and on-orbit checkout plans. Support launch operations, commissioning, and on-orbit GNC anomaly resolution. What You Bring to Portal Strong systems thinking across GNC, flight software, avionics, and test. Practical understanding of spacecraft attitude determination and control, sufficient to evaluate test results and diagnose anomalies. Discipline in requirements management, traceability, and configuration control. Hands-on approach to hardware integration and test, including lab and cleanroom work. Ability to coordinate across teams and drive open items to closure without direct authority. Clear written communication for test procedures, reports, and operations documentation. Basic Qualifications Bachelor's degree in Aerospace, Mechanical, Electrical, or Systems Engineering, or a related field. Minimum of 6 years of experience in spacecraft GNC, systems engineering, or integration and test. Experience owning requirements flow-down and verification for a spacecraft subsystem. Hands-on experience integrating and testing GNC sensors and actuators. Experience with FlatSat, software-in-the-loop, or hardware-in-the-loop test environments. Experience participating in spacecraft environmental testing, including TVAC. Proficiency in Python or MATLAB for test automation and data analysis. Preferred Qualifications Master's degree in Aerospace or Systems Engineering, or a related field. Experience with requirements management tools such as Jama, DOORS, or Polarion. Experience developing flight rules, operations procedures, and on-orbit checkout plans. On-orbit operations or commissioning experience. Experience with propulsion system integration and test. Experience with GNC fault management design and verification. Familiarity with spacecraft command and telemetry systems such as OpenC3 COSMOS performance assessment. Pay Range: $150,000–$205,000 Compensation And Benefits Your actual level and base salary will be determined on a case-by-case basis and may vary based on the following considerations: job-related knowledge and skills, education, and experience. At Portal, your base salary is just one part of your total rewards package. You may also be eligible for long-term incentives, in the form of company equity at an exciting time of company growth as well as potential bonuses. You will also receive access to comprehensive medical, vision, and dental coverage (premiums paid by Portal 100%), access to a 401(k)-retirement plan, paid parental leave, you may also accrue 3 weeks of paid vacation and will be eligible for 12 or more paid holidays per year as well as sick time. Eligibility to access ITAR-controlled items requires that candidates be U.S. persons , which includes U.S. citizens, lawful permanent residents, and other protected individuals as defined by U.S. law. Employment is contingent upon verification of ITAR eligibility and, where applicable, obtaining any required export authorization or license.
